claim: For the depth-p QAOA applied to MaxCut on large-girth (D+1)-regular graphs, in the limit D -> infinity, the cut fraction is 1/2 + nu_p(gamma,beta)/sqrt(D), where nu_p is given by the paper's infinite-D G-matrix iteration (equivalently, the QAOA energy density on the SK model). The tested result is the optimum bar_nu_p = max over (gamma,beta) of nu_p for depths p = 1 to 8.

quantities.description: bar_nu_1 = max over gamma in R^1, beta in R^1 of nu_1(gamma,beta). Here nu_p(gamma,beta) = lim_{D->inf} nu_p(D,gamma,beta) = (i/2) sum_{j=-p..p} Gamma_j (G^{(p)}_{0,j})^2. Index vectors as (a_1..a_p, a_0, a_{-p}..a_{-1}), with a_i in {+1,-1}. Gamma_r = gamma_r, Gamma_0 = 0, Gamma_{-r} = -gamma_r. f(a) = (1/2) <a_1|e^{i beta_1 X}|a_2> ... <a_p|e^{i beta_p X}|a_0> <a_0|e^{-i beta_p X}|a_{-p}> ... <a_{-2}|e^{-i beta_1 X}|a_{-1}>, where <a|e^{i beta X}|b> = cos(beta) if a=b and i sin(beta) otherwise. G^{(0)}_{jk} = sum_a f(a) a_j a_k. G^{(m)}_{jk} = sum_a f(a) a_j a_k exp(-(1/2) sum_{j',k'} G^{(m-1)}_{j'k'} Gamma_{j'} Gamma_{k'} a_{j'} a_{k'}) for m = 1..p. The cost driver is C = -(1/sqrt(D)) sum_{edges} Z_u Z_v. Report the global maximum at full precision. The result equals the SK-model QAOA energy V_p maximized over parameters.
bar_nu_2 = max over gamma, beta in R^2 of nu_2(gamma,beta), using the same infinite-D iteration and definitions as nu_bar_p1 with p = 2. Report the global maximum at full precision.
